assessment.nobel_worthiness: A formally adventurous bilingual body of fiction, poetry, essays and drama makes linguistic estrangement a continuing source of imaginative invention.
assessment.attribution: Yoko Tawada alone is credited for an oeuvre spanning Japanese and German literary practice, including The Emissary and Memoirs of a Polar Bear.
assessment.maturity: Its range across forms and sustained attention to language, migration and perception give the work substantial depth and an apt scope for recognition.
uncertainties: Assessment depends partly on translated access to work across two writing languages and several genres.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The densely patterned, visionary prose of Blinding and Solenoid presents an unusually ambitious metaphysical project centered on memory, body and imagination.
assessment.attribution: Mircea Cărtărescu alone is credited for this Romanian-language fictional and poetic oeuvre.
assessment.maturity: The recurrence and development of its imaginative system across a substantial body of work indicate sustained artistic purpose.
uncertainties: The relative force of the Romanian prose beyond available translations remains uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Interlinked narratives combine inventive storytelling with communal memory, legal power and Indigenous historical experience without reducing fiction to testimony.
assessment.attribution: Louise Erdrich alone is credited for fiction and poetry including Love Medicine and The Night Watchman.
assessment.maturity: A long, interconnected oeuvre has developed social worlds and narrative relations with notable continuity and breadth.
uncertainties: The assessment cannot establish equal familiarity with the full poetry and fiction corpus.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental fiction, poetry and archival nonfiction productively question authorship, violence and the recovery of lives excluded from official record.
assessment.attribution: Cristina Rivera Garza alone is credited for the multigenre Spanish- and English-language oeuvre represented by No One Will See Me Cry and Liliana’s Invincible Summer.
assessment.maturity: The work's formal range and recurring ethical inquiry support a broad citation rather than recognition for one title.
uncertainties: The balance of achievement across the Spanish and English work requires fuller corpus coverage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large polyphonic novels remake narrative scale through Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time, with conspicuous formal ambition.
assessment.attribution: Alexis Wright alone is credited for the fiction and nonfiction corpus including Carpentaria and The Swan Book.
assessment.maturity: The major novels suggest a coherent and developing project of considerable imaginative and historical reach.
uncertainties: A fuller assessment would require more complete coverage beyond the representative major works.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large poetic sequences and landscape-scale interventions create a distinctive collective memorial language from suffering and historical violence.
assessment.attribution: Raúl Zurita alone is credited for the Spanish-language poetry represented by Purgatory and Anteparadise.
assessment.maturity: The sustained scale of the poetic project and its formal continuity indicate an oeuvre of durable consequence.
uncertainties: The sonic, visual and formal dimensions of the Spanish poetry may be incompletely carried by translation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Radical narrative structures connect bodily experience to dictatorship and social exclusion through a distinctive, difficult formal practice.
assessment.attribution: Diamela Eltit alone is credited for Spanish-language fiction and essays including E. Luminata and The Fourth World.
assessment.maturity: The enduring interrogation of power through changing experimental forms suggests a sustained rather than episodic achievement.
uncertainties: Translation availability and incomplete access to the full Spanish-language oeuvre limit comparative judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A desert cosmology joins Tuareg experience, ecological limits and metaphysical fiction in a literary world of unusual imaginative coherence.
assessment.attribution: Ibrahim al-Koni alone is credited for the Arabic-language fiction represented by Gold Dust and The Bleeding of the Stone.
assessment.maturity: The recurrent landscape, philosophical pressure and cultural specificity point to a substantial, sustained novelistic achievement.
uncertainties: The assessment is constrained by translation and by limited direct coverage of the larger Arabic corpus.
